channel.description: Recent content in Fascism on MoscowMigrant

item.title: The Elite Fracture: Arrests, 'Suicides,' and the Crisis at the Top
item.description: Russia's ruling class is being thinned out by three distinct kinds of misfortune at once — corruption arrests, murky 'suicides,' and targeted eliminations — and together they amount to a genuine crisis at the top of a regime that has chosen wartime theft over national prosperity.

item.title: The Imperial Syndrome Is a Treatable Disease, Not a Russian Gene
item.description: Russians are an imperial people, but imperialism is a socio-cultural condition carried by an inherited cultural code, not by biology. Talk of a Russian "slavery gene" is racial theory in a new coat — and the proof it can be cured is that some Russians have already broken free.

item.title: The Return of Stalin: A State-Assisted Cult and the Red-Brown Synthesis
item.description: Over thirty-five years, Russia has staged a state-assisted revival of the Stalin cult — and Stalinism has now overtaken the very Putinism that resurrected it, fusing the Communist Party and Putin's fascism into a single red-brown identity.

item.title: Iran and Israel: Why Aggressor and Defender Are Not Symmetrical
item.description: When a war breaks out, the easiest and most flattering reflex is to declare both sides equally guilty. But moral symmetry between Iran and Israel is a falsehood, and facts, not feelings, are what determine political truth.

item.title: There Is No 'Other, Beautiful Russia': War Forces You to Choose a Side
item.description: In peacetime you can be against the regime and still vaguely "for the country." War abolishes that comfort. It poses one question—whose side are you on?—and there is no honest way to answer it while refusing to help the country being bombed.

item.title: The Suppression Machine: How Dictatorships Manufacture Obedience
item.description: A dictator commands no superpowers, yet millions obey. The answer lies not in the people's character but in a machine of suppression, negative selection, and institutionalized distrust that isolates every individual against the whole.

item.title: Collective Responsibility Is Real, But Guilt Is Always Individual
item.description: An argument that the idea of collective guilt is a road to fascism and Bolshevism, while collective responsibility is genuine and unavoidable — and that only a careful, differentiated separation of criminals, combatants, propagandists, and the merely responsible makes justice possible.

item.title: America Against Itself: A Democracy Resisting Its Own Fascist Leader
item.description: The United States has entered a strange intermediate condition: a genuinely free country governed by a clique with dictatorial ambitions. Unlike disarmed Russia, America still has courts, states, a free press, and an armed citizenry — which is why the outcome of this fight is genuinely open.

item.title: Europe Is the Real Growth-Point of Resistance
item.description: As America retreats from its role as guarantor of the free world, the decisive force standing against both Putinism and Trumpism is neither China nor a revived NATO but Europe itself — and the popular charge that Europe "never came to Ukraine's war" collapses the moment you examine it honestly.

item.title: Creeping Munich: A Betrayal That Cannot Be Consummated
item.description: The West is repeating the error of 1938 against Ukraine, but in slow motion and never completed: a betrayal that proceeds as a fact yet cannot reach its consummation, because Ukraine is not Czechoslovakia and refuses to surrender.

item.title: There Is No Perfect Constitution: Why Systems Must Fit Their Societies
item.description: A reflection on why no electoral system, state structure, or constitution is universally ideal: universal principles are real, but the deep question is always how far a society's socio-cultural base contradicts its institutions. One size fits no one.

item.title: Who Actually Supports This War: The Politics of Passive Complicity
item.description: An attempt to count, honestly, who stands behind the war against Ukraine — and to show why the silent majority's head-in-the-sand stance amounts, politically, to support, even as it differs morally from the howling of the propagandists.

item.title: Russia Cannot Be Reformed Within Its Borders: The Case for Imperial Collapse
item.description: An argument that Russia is an empire pregnant with disintegration, that no reform can make it normal within its present borders, and that only full collapse — including its ethnic Russian core — can finally cure the imperial syndrome.

item.title: Luck, Not Merit: The Accidental Architecture of Putin's Power
item.description: A quarter-century of one man's rule looks less like the achievement of a statesman than a long, improbable streak of fortunate accidents — and accidents, by their nature, eventually stop coming.

item.title: An Idea Is Not an Ideology: Why the 'Russian World' Cannot Reshape History
item.description: Putin and Trump cannot bend history the way Lenin or Genghis Khan did, because they have only power and money where those figures had a guiding idea. The "Russian world" is an idea, but never an ideology — it points only backward, which is why no one else has ever adopted it.

item.title: Negotiating With a Predator: Why Talks With Russia Are Structurally Impossible
item.description: Every round of talks with Putin's Russia is a performance staged for a single overseas spectator and a smokescreen for the killing that continues underneath. You cannot negotiate while waging war, and Moscow's true precondition is not a compromise but the disappearance of Ukraine as a state.

item.title: Symbols Grow From Flawed Soil: Judging People by Direction, Not Purity
item.description: Why the symbols of a free society are legitimate despite their flaws: they grow from the same imperfect soil as everything else, and what matters is the direction a person leads their society, not the impossible standard of personal purity.

item.title: Russia Has Never Had a Free Press: Propaganda Is Not Journalism
item.description: Russia's press was never an information service; it was born as an instrument of propaganda. And propaganda, being a chemical blow to public consciousness, is not journalism at all but something closer to a controlled substance.

item.title: The Stylistics of Neo-Fascism: Why Style Reveals More Than Politics
item.description: Trump and Putin quarrel over Ukraine, yet beneath the friction they share a single style of boorish triumphalism, pious cruelty, and atrophied empathy. That style, not any policy, is the true signature of neo-fascism — and it is winning.

item.title: Chaos as a Product: How Trump Governs and Who Benefits
item.description: Trump's presidency does not produce a strategy; it produces chaos. This essay argues that the swings, the broken promises, and the endless "two more weeks" are not a hidden plan but the product itself, and that in the short term the confusion serves the man who manufactures death.

item.title: The Collapse of the Post-War Order and the Birth of a European Civilization
item.description: The transatlantic order built on Germany's 1945 surrender is dissolving in real time, a rupture on the scale of 1945 and 1991. The right response is not despair but the consolidation of Europe into a sovereign civilization with its own arms and its own will.

item.title: The War Will Be Decided on the Battlefield, Not at the Table
item.description: Why this war has a military solution and not a diplomatic one — and why the only honest road to peace runs through arming Ukraine, exhausting Russia's war machine, and carrying the fight to military targets on Russian soil.

item.title: Democracies Win the Marathon: The Illusion of Authoritarian Efficiency
item.description: Authoritarian power looks invincible in the short term and collapses in the long one. This essay argues that democracy is a marathon runner, not a sprinter, and that its right to defend itself against extremists is no betrayal of its principles but a condition of its survival.

item.title: The Brown International: A Transnational Far-Right Movement Filling a Void
item.description: A coordinated far-right international has consolidated across borders, rallying around figures like Le Pen. It wins not through a coherent program but through energy and grievance, because fascism behaves like a gas that fills any void left by an exhausted liberalism.

item.title: Postmodern Fascism: Trumpism as a New Form of the Old Disease
item.description: Trumpism is not ordinary right-wing populism but a postmodern mutation of fascism, built on lying without precedent and the open contempt for empathy — and it is uniquely dangerous because it has captured a still-free democracy.

item.title: Words Are Deeds: Against the Counsel to Ignore What Leaders Say
item.description: A defense of taking political rhetoric seriously: the words of the powerful are themselves a material force that moves markets, launders aggression, and reshapes what people plan and do. The fashionable advice to judge leaders only by deeds is not worldly wisdom but a disarming mistake.

item.title: Twin Brothers: Why Trump and Putin Reinforce Each Other Without a Pact
item.description: The popular theory that Trump is a recruited Kremlin agent requires a secret folder no one has ever produced. A far simpler explanation fits every fact: he and Putin are ideological twins whose interests converge on their own.

item.title: The Russian Liberation Army the West Refuses to Build
item.description: There is a way to end this war from within Russia, and it is staring everyone in the face: alongside fully arming Ukraine, build a serious Russian Volunteer Liberation Army from the units already fighting. It fails not for feasibility but for three missing political wills.

item.title: A Monster Civilization: Russia's Cultural Suicide
item.description: Russia is not a self-standing 'separate civilization' but a derivative one — a non-self-sufficient offshoot of Europe that borrowed its culture and then turned against the parent. In this war it has committed cultural suicide: cancelling itself abroad, gutting the institutions a living culture needs, grafting Soviet archaism onto fascism, and producing death instead of life. Subtract Europe and the 'dry residue' is not a civilization at all but a monster.

item.title: Antisemitism: The Attribute of Crystallizing Fascism
item.description: The Russian regime's antisemitism is read as a string of embarrassing slips. It is the opposite: a structural attribute that fascism inevitably acquires as it hardens, as reliable a diagnostic as any. A regime that runs on hatred needs a personified internal enemy, and when the convenient enemies are used up it reaches for the oldest Other — a hatred that needs no real object at all. The same machine is now reappearing in the West as the Holocaust's immunity wears off.
